speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand the progression of your symptoms: did your right leg weakness and unsteady gait start before or after the forgetfulness and paranoid behavior began?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Progressive Aphasia with frontotemporal dementia progression? No, let me re-evaluate. The combination of progressive cognitive decline (memory loss, getting lost, apraxia) over 6 months followed by acute neurological deficits (weakness, falls) in a 44-year-old male is highly concerning for a space-occupying lesion causing increased intracranial pressure or direct compression. I need to see the brain structure immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Complementary_Coagulation_Profile.
